ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks the matrix on fresh P after a read of Q. It does not establish the promise that the API decides each action by the caller's role on the project after earlier requests to P.

objections.objection: The API can allow a viewer's second comment request. This violates 'Every other pairing of role and action is refused' while all criteria pass.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the second comment request returns 2xx and adds a comment despite the caller remaining a viewer.
scenario.given: The API correctly handles every tested first request, but a refused comment request incorrectly caches permission to comment on P.
scenario.when: A viewer sends two comment requests to the same existing project without changing roles.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks allowed effects against the freshly seeded state. It does not discharge the same effects after the project has changed through allowed actions.

objections.objection: An allowed comment can replace an existing comment once P already has three comments. This violates 'an allowed comment adds the comment to it'.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the second added comment replaces the first added comment instead of being appended.
scenario.given: Comment insertion appends correctly when P has its two seeded comments, but overwrites the last comment when P has three.
scenario.when: A commenter successfully adds two comments to the same project.

ground.reason: PRM-A1 checks refusal responses after the preceding read of Q. PRM-A2 checks preservation rather than the refusal response. Neither establishes the specified response for a refusal without that preceding read.

objections.objection: A refused action can return HTTP 401 before any read of Q. This violates 'A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body {"error": "forbidden"}'.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the viewer's refused delete returns HTTP 401 instead of the specified HTTP 403 and body.
scenario.given: The API preserves P on every refusal, but initializes the required refusal response only after the caller has read Q.
scenario.when: A viewer sends delete to P without first reading Q.

ground.reason: PRM-A2 checks preservation on freshly seeded P. It does not establish preservation after P has changed through an allowed action.

objections.objection: A refused edit can restore the seeded body after an owner has edited P. This violates 'A refused action leaves the project as it was'.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the refused edit returns the specified 403 while changing P's body back to its seeded value.
scenario.given: Refused edits restore the seeded body, which leaves every freshly seeded project unchanged.
scenario.when: An owner edits P's body, then a viewer sends a refused edit to that same project.

ground.reason: PRM-A3 always precedes the no-role request with a read of Q. D3 promises the absent-project response for each action without imposing that prerequisite.

objections.objection: A first no-role request can reveal that P exists. This violates 'the same response a request for a project that does not exist gets'.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the no-role read returns 403 while the corresponding absent-project read returns 404.
scenario.given: The API produces indistinguishable responses after a read of Q, but returns 403 for an existing project before that setup.
scenario.when: The user with no role on P reads P without first reading Q.

ground.reason: PRM-A3 checks preservation only after a read of Q. It does not establish D3's unconditional promise that 'The project is unchanged'.

objections.objection: A no-role request without the preceding read of Q can mutate P while returning the correct absent-project response.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but an owner's subsequent read shows that P's revision list has changed.
scenario.given: No-role requests preserve P after a read of Q, but append a revision before returning the absent-project response when that read has not occurred.
scenario.when: The user with no role on P sends edit without first reading Q.

obligations.statement: For callers with a role, authorization uses their role on the target project and follows the complete D1 matrix.
obligations.source: What changes: 'The project API decides each of its four actions by the caller's role on the project, as the matrix in D1 gives.' D1: 'A viewer may read. A commenter may read and comment. An owner may do all four. Every other pairing of role and action is refused.'

parts.statement: The twelve role/action pairings follow D1 on freshly seeded P after the caller reads Q.
The same authorization matrix holds for other request histories, including subsequent requests to P.

obligations.statement: Allowed reads return the project, comments add the submitted comment, edits replace the body with the submitted body, and deletes remove the project.
obligations.source: D1: 'An allowed read returns the project, an allowed comment adds the comment to it, an allowed edit replaces its body with the one sent, and an allowed delete removes it.'

parts.statement: Each allowed action produces its specified effect on freshly seeded P in PRM-A1's scenarios.
Allowed actions produce the same specified effects on existing projects after earlier allowed actions have changed their contents.

obligations.statement: An action refused under the role matrix returns HTTP 403 with the specified forbidden body.
obligations.source: D2: 'A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body {"error": "forbidden"}'.

parts.statement: Every refused role/action pairing returns the specified response on freshly seeded P after the caller reads Q.
Every refused role/action pairing returns the specified response under other request histories, including without a preceding read of Q.

obligations.statement: A refused action preserves the project as subsequently observed by an owner.
obligations.source: What changes: 'A refused action leaves the project as it was.' D2: 'the project, as an owner reads it afterwards, is unchanged.'

parts.statement: The refused D1 pairings preserve freshly seeded P's title, body, comments and revision list in PRM-A2's scenarios.
Refused actions also preserve those project fields under other request histories and project states, including after an allowed edit.

obligations.statement: For every action, a caller with no role receives the corresponding absent-project response, with only Date and X-Request-Id values permitted to differ and their formats preserved, while the project remains unchanged.
obligations.source: D3: 'A caller with no role on the project gets, for each of the four actions, the same response a request for a project that does not exist gets, apart from the values of the Date and X-Request-Id headers, which have the same format as for a project that does not exist. The project is unchanged.'

parts.statement: Each no-role action has the specified response equivalence on freshly seeded P after the caller reads Q.
Each no-role action preserves freshly seeded P as observed by an owner after the caller reads Q.
The specified no-role response equivalence also holds under other request histories, including without a preceding read of Q.
No-role actions also preserve P under other request histories, including without a preceding read of Q.

rejected.objection: The API can allow a viewer's second comment request.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: a further repetition of a refused request, a behaviour PRM-A1 and PRM-A2 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.

rejected.objection: An allowed comment can replace an existing comment once P already has three comments.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: another comment count, a behaviour PRM-A1 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.

rejected.objection: A refused action can return HTTP 401 before any read of Q.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: another ordering of requests, without the read of Q, a behaviour PRM-A1 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.

rejected.objection: A refused edit can restore the seeded body after an owner has edited P.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: another ordering of requests, after an owner's edit, a behaviour PRM-A2 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.

rejected.objection: A first no-role request can reveal that P exists.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: another ordering of requests, without the read of Q, a behaviour PRM-A3 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.

rejected.objection: A no-role request without the preceding read of Q can mutate P while returning the correct absent-project response.
rejected.reason: Rejected as a variant of an observed case: another ordering of requests, without the read of Q, a behaviour PRM-A3 observes; the standard does not demand exhaustive testing, and the objection names no promise that no criterion observes.
